subject.title: feat: replace legacy exec approvals with V2

question: Should upgrades preserve existing V1 approval constraints through a constrained compatibility or migration path, or should this PR intentionally retire all V1 allow and deny decisions and require operator reapproval?
rationale: The branch changes persisted security policy semantics and breaks established invocation shapes; source evidence cannot determine whether that upgrade cost is an accepted product and security tradeoff.

options.title: Require a compatible upgrade path
options.body: Keep existing V1 constraints effective until users complete a visible V2 migration or reapproval flow, while preserving canonical argv at the execution boundary.

options.title: Approve the intentional cutover
options.body: Accept that V1 rules and raw string callers stop working after upgrade, with prominent release and recovery guidance for affected operators.

options.title: Split the transition
options.body: Land V2 internals behind compatibility adapters first, then schedule the breaking policy and API cutover in a separately approved release.

recommendation.title: Require a compatible upgrade path
recommendation.body: Keep existing V1 constraints effective until users complete a visible V2 migration or reapproval flow, while preserving canonical argv at the execution boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged V2 approval-dialog work is the direct foundation for the authorization and presentation model this PR promotes to the default path.
